title: Module capabilities and derived artifacts
objective: Trim the module capabilities framework to what its recorded decisions require: resources installed from their pinned URL only, grants that evict instead of refusing at the cap, artifacts collected, the transport on ureq's own agent in a crate of its own, activation deferred until a module needs it, a desktop surface sized to what a person must see, and each behaviour tested at one level.
context_summary: The framework (settings and profiles, Keychain secrets, per-asset consent, the capability worker, verified resource installs, tasks and derived artifacts) has one consumer, the developer proof module; at the 2026-09-26 review it cost about 15.6k shipped lines, 43 packages and about 4.3 MB of the executable. The owner kept it on 2026-09-24 and on 2026-09-26 trimmed it further. Waves 1 and 2 landed resource installs from the pinned URL only, grant eviction at the record cap, artifact collection and the transport on `ureq`'s own agent. What remains is activation deferred, the desktop surface trimmed, the transport and Keychain store in a crate of their own, the leftovers and the duplicate tests. Artifacts travel on the recipe, settings, grants and installed resources share one document store, settings use the parameter vocabulary, capability jobs are records in the one job table and publish to the activity board. Decisions: docs/decisions.md "Module capabilities", "Architecture review" and "Post-consolidation review"; design: docs/design/module-capabilities.md; constraints: docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Remove the local-file source from `module.resource.install`, so a resource installs only from its pinned URL and no client can make the owner read a path.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. The agent contract says a live-session client can never grant itself access to files, networks or photos (docs/design/architecture.md); the file install source lets any client do exactly the first of those.

`InstallSource::File { path }` (`crates/luxforge-core/src/capabilities/resources.rs`) needs no grant, and the host's file arm (`crates/luxforge-core/src/capabilities/host/resources.rs`) only checks that the given path is a readable file before queuing `copy_local`, with no permission-authority check at all. When the copied file is shorter than the resource's pinned size, `stage_and_publish` (`resources.rs`) reports "`<id> is <length> bytes; it is pinned at <bytes> bytes`", handing the caller the exact length of whatever it pointed at.

No production module uses the file source; only `lifecycle_tests.rs` (its `install_from_file` helper, four call sites) and one call in `proof_tests.rs` do, and the same test file already runs a loopback `TestServer` (`serving()`) that answers `/palette` and `/swatch` with the pinned bytes for other install tests, so those tests can download from it instead.
docs/design/module-capabilities.md's Lifecycle section and docs/user-guide.md both still document `source: {kind: "file", path}` as a supported, grant-free install path and need to drop it.
Current shapes only: `source: {kind: "file", ...}` becomes an unrecognized field, refused like any other malformed parameter, not a soft deprecation.

tasks.description: At the grant cap, evict the oldest live remote-image-request grant instead of refusing a new one, and have `module.status` report grant and denial counts rather than every record.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. Consent is per asset by decision (docs/decisions.md, Module capabilities), so work that sends many photos leaves one live grant per photo and nothing today ever retires one.

`Document::make_room` (`crates/luxforge-core/src/capabilities/grants.rs`, `MAX_GRANT_RECORDS = 1024`) prunes only the oldest revoked grant or denial, and once every record is a live grant it refuses with "1024 live grants are recorded; revoke one before granting another" while the desktop can only revoke grants one at a time. A `Grant` already carries `created_ms` and its `kind` (`DownloadArtifact` or `RemoteImageRequest`), enough to find the oldest live remote-image grant without touching a download grant.

Every remote-image requirement check reads the whole grants file (`CapabilityHost::status` and a task's own consent check in `capabilities/host/tasks.rs` both load the full document), and `module.status`'s `permissions` field ships that whole `GrantList` back to every caller, including the desktop after every round trip (`crates/luxforge-app/src/state/capabilities.rs`'s `ModuleStatus.permissions: GrantList`).

The existing bound test in `grants.rs` fills the file with 1,024 live `download-artifact` grants and expects a refusal; that must keep refusing, since there is no live remote-image grant to evict and a download grant is never evicted. Eviction only fires when a live remote-image grant exists to take its place.

docs/design/module-capabilities.md's grants-bound sentence (Capability and consent contract) states the 1,024-record bound but not what happens there; it should say the oldest live remote-image grant is evicted and asked for again.

tasks.description: Collect unreferenced derived artifacts once when a catalog opens, on the source worker, instead of only through an explicit call nothing makes today.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. The recipe-carried artifact table itself is already correct and complete; what is missing is ever running the collection that depends on it.

`EditorService::plan_collection` (`crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/artifact_store.rs`) deletes unreferenced, non-live rows in one owner transaction and returns a `Collection`; `artifact_collect` (`crates/luxforge-core/src/api/owner.rs`) queues it as `SourceTaskKind::Collect`, which the source worker runs as `artifacts::collect_files`, listing and removing the orphaned object files. Nothing outside tests calls `artifact_collect` today.

The proposed Corrections module would publish several disposable multi-megabyte candidates per AI Remove generation and keep only the one a person accepts (docs/design/corrections.md); under today's contract every candidate stays a catalog artifact until something collects it.

Queue the existing `plan_collection`/`artifact_collect` path once when the owner opens a catalog (`Owner::launch`, `crates/luxforge-core/src/api/owner.rs`), not on every action afterwards. Returning Corrections' own disposable candidates as bounded job results instead of catalog artifacts is that milestone's own later work, not this task's.

tasks.description: Spike `ureq`'s own agent behind the address policy and prove that cancelling a stalled request by shutting its socket down works through rustls.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. The owner's 2026-09-24 decision to move the transport onto a well-known HTTP client did not land in substance: the change kept a hand-written resolver, socket, TLS session, read/write loop and framing, and only handed request-head writing and response parsing to `ureq-proto`, so the client shrank from 1,098 to 1,079 lines while gaining four packages.

docs/design/module-capabilities.md's Transport section records why: `ureq`'s connector, transport and resolver must be `'static`, so a request run inside its own call could reach a borrowed cancel only through a watcher thread or an owned handle. The job's `JobControl` (`crates/luxforge-core/src/capabilities/jobs.rs`) is already `Arc`-shared between the owner and the worker, so an owned cancel handle costs nothing to build; this spike is what proves whether it actually stops a stalled read.

Confirmed in the pinned `ureq` 3.4.2 source: `Agent::with_parts(config, connector, resolver)` (`agent.rs:130`) takes any `impl Connector` and `impl Resolver`, `Resolver` is a public trait, and connectors chain (`Connector::chain`) so a policy-driven `TcpTransport::new(stream, buffers)` can feed a `RustlsConnector` built with `RootCerts::PlatformVerifier` or `RootCerts::Specific` and an injected crypto provider, under the real `rustls-no-provider` and `platform-verifier` feature flags. `Config` already exposes `proxy(None)`, `max_redirects(0)`, `max_response_header_size`, `max_idle_connections(0)`, a timeout per phase and a body `limit()` reader.

Today's transport already has the policy logic a `ureq` adapter must preserve: `capabilities/transport/net.rs`'s `Resolve`/`Connect` traits and its `connect` function resolve a host once, check every address against `policy::address_allowed` for the endpoint's class, and connect only to a checked address.
This is a throwaway spike on a branch or scratch worktree, not the production change: TASK-005 does the real deletion and rewrite once this confirms the approach, or is cancelled if it does not.

tasks.description: Run the module transport on `ureq`'s agent behind the unchanged address policy, deleting the hand-written exchange loop, and pin `idna_adapter` so endpoint parsing adds no Unicode data stack.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. This lands the 2026-09-24 decision; the spike (`capabilities/transport/ureq_spike.rs`, recorded in docs/design/module-capabilities.md's Transport section) confirmed resolve-once policy, prompt socket-shutdown cancellation and the TLS behaviour on `ureq` 3.4.2's agent.

Today's client is `capabilities/transport/exchange.rs` (550 lines), `mod.rs` (352), `net.rs` (105) and `tls.rs` (72) — its own resolution, socket, rustls session, a read/write loop that wakes every 100 ms so cancellation can be checked between reads, buffering, interim-response skipping, redirects and framing stricter than `ureq-proto`'s own. Replace it with one `ureq::Agent` per request (`Agent::with_parts`) built as the spike built it: the policy `Resolver` over `Resolve`, a policy `Connector` over `Connect` with Luxforge's own socket transport (ureq 3.4.2's `TcpTransport` is not exported) that registers a cloned socket with the job's `JobControl` so `cancel()` shuts it down, and Luxforge's own TLS transport on `tls::client_config`, never ureq's `RustlsConnector`, whose body handler takes rustls' `UnexpectedEof` on a connection closed without `close_notify` as the end of a close-delimited body and so accepts a truncated TLS body. No proxy, no pool, statuses as data, `max_redirects(0)`, a 64 KiB head limit and identity encoding; keep the existing redirect check and loop over at most three redirects; stream the body through `limit(max)` and report progress from that loop instead of per chunk.

A cancel overrides a success: a shut-down plain socket reads as the end of a close-delimited body, so the transport checks the job's cancel before reporting a body complete, as the spike's `spike_cancelling_a_stalled_close_delimited_body_is_not_taken_for_its_end` proves. `ureq`'s timeouts are per phase, not today's idle timeout between reads, so the socket transport applies the idle read timeout itself; and the response framing today's exchange refuses but `ureq-proto` accepts (a bare LF, the header field cap) is either kept by the transport or its loss is recorded in the Transport section. The spike module and its dev-dependency go when this lands; its tests become the transport's.
Keep `policy.rs` unchanged, and keep the transport's structured error kinds (`validation`, `resource-limit`, `read-error`, `cancelled`) exactly as they are; only message wording may change.

`idna_adapter` is pinned at 1.2.2 today through `url = "=2.5.8"`, used only by `capabilities/descriptor.rs` and the transport. Pinning `idna_adapter = "=1.0.0"` drops its ICU4X back end: a non-ASCII endpoint host is refused by name while punycode keeps working. `ureq` needs its own address parsing regardless, so this is independent cleanup riding along with the transport change, not a consequence of it.

Add a `check-repository` boundary rule (`xtask/src/repository.rs`'s forbidden-token table) that refuses `ureq_proto::` and `httparse::` outside `capabilities/transport/`, so a second hand-written HTTP framing implementation can never reappear elsewhere. No render or export path is touched; only the transport's tests, the capability proof's network calls and the capabilities smoke exercise this code.

Delivered on ureq 3.4.2's agent with Luxforge's own resolver, connector, socket and TLS transports; the client is about 1,150 lines, not the roughly 700 fewer the estimate assumed, because ureq makes the caller supply all four. Recorded with the framing decision in docs/design/module-capabilities.md's Transport section.

tasks.description: Defer the activation lifecycle until a module needs `local-runtime`, deleting `module.activate`, `module.deactivate` and their job kinds, admission rules and hooks.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Activation's only real consumer is preloading a local model using a cancellable worker (docs/design/corrections.md), which is the `local-runtime` capability the owner's decisions already defer until its first consumer.

`capabilities/host/activation.rs` (424 lines) implements `inactive`/`activating`/`active`/`failed` states, a pending-deactivation-while-activating flag and supersede-versus-cancel. The one job table (`jobs.rs`) carries `JobKind::Activate` and `JobKind::Deactivate` on the module lane and `Admission::Always`, which only a deactivation uses; `Jobs::supersede` stays, because the analysis path also supersedes pending jobs. `capabilities/descriptor.rs` validates an `ActivationDescriptor`, a setting can declare `invalidates_activation` (`capabilities/settings.rs`), `module.status` reports an `activation` block, and a `requires_active` task fails with an `activation` requirement (`host/tasks.rs`).

The proof module's `activate()` (`modules/capabilities_proof.rs`) reads a 20-byte palette, then sleeps out an artificial `activation_delay` in 10 ms checkpoints purely so the cancel path has something to test; its task refuses until that palette is loaded. Tasks already read installed resources through their own context (`ModuleContext::resource_path`, `capabilities/context.rs`) with no dependency on activation, so the proof task's palette read moves there with no new mechanism.

Beyond the core: the desktop's Activate control and its message, the evidence script's `activate` capability step (`CapabilityAction::Activate` in `luxforge-evidence`), the `capabilities` smoke's `activated` step and `luxforge-app/tests/json_cli.rs`'s `module.activate` case all go with it.

docs/design/module-capabilities.md's Lifecycle, jobs and resources section, docs/design/develop-workspace.md's tool-array row for the capability block (which also still names `module.job.*`), docs/features.md's capability row and docs/user-guide.md's `module.activate`/`deactivate` paragraph all describe activation as shipped today; each needs to say it returns with `local-runtime` instead.

Current shapes only: this removes two API methods, two job kinds, the `activation` requirement kind and `module.status`'s activation block from `schema.list`, not a soft deprecation. No render path is touched. The module contract's developer-only test modules also change how the proof module registers; whichever lands second follows the other.

tasks.description: Move the TLS transport and the Keychain secret store out of `luxforge-core` into a crate the desktop and `luxforge-json` inject through `HostConfig`, behind a core-owned transport trait, so the core and its test binaries link no TLS or Security framework.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. The transport is settled on `ureq`'s own agent (`capabilities/transport/agent.rs`), so this moves the finished code once.

`crates/luxforge-core/Cargo.toml` lists `rustls` (with `ring`), `rustls-platform-verifier`, `ureq` and `ureq-proto` as plain dependencies, and `security-framework` under the macOS target, unconditionally, so they compile into `luxforge-core`'s one rlib and link every one of its test binaries, including render, mask and history tests that never touch a module capability.

The seam is half there. `SecretStore` (`capabilities/secrets.rs`) is already a trait `HostConfig` takes as `Arc<dyn SecretStore>`: the Keychain store (`KeychainSecretStore`, `platform_secret_store`) moves out, and the trait, `MemorySecretStore` and `UnavailableSecretStore` stay. The transport is not injected yet: `HostConfig.transport` is a `TransportConfig` of `TlsTrust`, `Resolve` and `Connect` (`capabilities/transport/net.rs`), from which the core builds its own rustls `Transport` on first use (`SharedTransport`, `capabilities/resources.rs`). This task adds a core-owned trait for sending one checked request, which `HostConfig` takes and resource installs and `ModuleContext::send` call, with the rustls and `ureq` implementation in the new crate.

The address policy's endpoint parsing (`EndpointClass`, `parse_endpoint`, `capabilities/transport/policy.rs`) stays in the core, because both descriptor validators use it; the capability leftovers task moves it to a neutral module, and whichever of the two lands second follows the other.

The core's capability tests (`lifecycle_tests.rs`, `proof_tests.rs`, `context.rs`) run real TLS today, over loopback with `TlsTrust::Roots` and `luxforge-testkit`'s `TestServer`. They move to an in-memory implementation of the new trait, and `capabilities/transport/tests.rs` (about 1,275 lines) moves with the transport, so TLS stays tested where it lives. The `http-client-crates` and `http-framing` rows of `cargo xtask check-repository` name `luxforge-core` and its `capabilities/transport` directory as the only home of `ureq` and HTTP framing; they follow the move.

docs/design/architecture.md's Workspace section already states the principle this follows: "Add boundaries when there is real code to own them." Its `luxforge-core` bullet lists the capability host and its files as part of the core and needs updating once the transport and secrets move out. The desktop group's headless-binary crate, once it exists, is the other injector beside the desktop.

tasks.description: Clear the capability leftovers: a typed requirement kind, the removed file-kind remnants, write results nobody reads, duplicated formatting and parsing, and stale documentation.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure, swept up after the fixes and after activation is gone (this task depends on both) so it edits code that has already settled. None of these items changes behavior beyond refusing one setting shape nothing can use.

`Requirement.kind` (`capabilities/host.rs`) is a bare string whose own doc comment lists `setting`, `resource`, `activation` and `profile`, while docs/design/module-capabilities.md instead lists `setting|resource|activation|grant`; the code never emits `grant`, and the desktop's `"grant"` match arm (`state/capabilities.rs`) is dead. With activation gone, only `setting`, `resource` and `profile` remain possible: make the field an enum of those three and bring the doc in line with it.

A settings `file` parameter kind and its `read-user-file` capability were decided removed on 2026-09-24 because nothing used them, and the type itself is gone, but the wording survives: docs/decisions.md's "an endpoint or path change" phrase, a comment in `host.rs` saying a grant names its exact path, `context.rs`'s comment excluding "file paths" from a module's context values, an error string in `app/capabilities.rs` naming a "file" setting step, `view/capabilities.rs`'s doc comment about a native file dialog, and the settings test fixture (`settings.rs`) still writing an unused `input.bin`. This is a separate, already-decided removal from this plan's own resource-install source.

`SettingsWrite.previous` (`capabilities/settings.rs`) is built on every write and read only by tests; the requirement list that becomes a `not-ready` error is formatted in `host/activation.rs` and `host/tasks.rs`, and deferring activation removes one copy; `profile_status` hand-copies the serde field names once in `host/tasks.rs` and again in the desktop's `state/capabilities.rs`; io errors are mapped by four helpers (`atomic_file.rs`'s `file_error`, `capabilities/resources.rs`'s `write_failure`, `artifacts/store.rs`'s `access` and `editor/source.rs`'s `file_access`); and there are three `now_ms` helpers (`capabilities/grants.rs` returning `u64`, `artifacts/store.rs` and `editor/catalog.rs` returning `i64`).

`artifacts/store.rs`'s manifest reader (`root_state`) reads and checks its format-marked JSON by hand instead of through the shared `JsonDocument` that settings, grants and installed resources already use, and both `modules/descriptor.rs` (the module parameter vocabulary) and `capabilities/descriptor.rs` import `capabilities::transport::{EndpointClass, parse_endpoint}` directly; move those two items to a neutral module both can depend on, which also keeps them in the core when the transport moves to its own crate.

A module-level `endpoint` setting passes `capabilities/descriptor.rs`'s field validation today but nothing reads it, since `profile_endpoint` (`host.rs`) only reads profile-level fields, so it should be refused at registration instead of silently doing nothing. `context.rs`'s comment says a credential is cleared as soon as the request is done and zeroizes its own header copy, but the transport's prepared request (`prepare`, `capabilities/transport/mod.rs`) and `ureq`'s buffers hold further copies that are never zeroed; say "best effort", or zero those too. docs/features.md's long-running-work list omits capability jobs, which already publish to the activity board.

tasks.description: Test each capability behaviour at one level: fixture-level lifecycle tests own the behaviours, one core proof journey, one CLI authority test, one desktop consent-and-apply test and the smoke.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests, after activation and the desktop surface are trimmed so there is no dead-code coverage left to carry along.

Outcome: test lines fell by about 510 net (1,212 removed, 703 added, including about 220 lines of JsonDocument tests and the shared owner harness), short of the 1,000 to 1,300 estimated, because TASK-006 had already deleted the activation tests the estimate counted, the running-activation cancel pair among them. `luxforge-json`'s proof journey (`a_proof_endpoint_client_installs_runs_the_task_and_applies_its_tint`) is kept beside its authority test: it is the only process-level proof of the binary's `--proof-endpoint`, `--data-root` and `--secret-store` wiring over the real transport and of stderr carrying no key, so nothing at its layer proves it.

`app/capabilities_tests.rs`'s `capability_steps_parse_strictly_and_record_a_secret_as_redacted` and `luxforge-evidence/src/tests.rs`'s `capability_steps_round_trip_and_record_a_secret_as_redacted` run the same script (settings, secret, profile, install, remove, task, consent, apply, cancel, revoke) and assert the same redaction; keep the evidence crate's version and delete the app's copy.

The same behaviours are proved on both the fixture module and the proof module: endpoint revocation (`changing_what_a_grant_names_revokes_it` in `lifecycle_tests.rs`, `changing_the_endpoint_revokes_its_grant_and_asks_for_consent_again` in `proof_tests.rs`) and removing a required resource (`removing_a_required_resource_deactivates_the_module_and_deletes_only_the_resource`, `removing_the_resource_deactivates_the_module_and_the_accepted_tint_still_renders`); the running-activation cancel pair goes with activation. Besides the proof module there are five fake capability modules: `LifecycleModule` (`capabilities/testing.rs`), `Publisher` (`proof_tests.rs`), `TintModule` (`artifacts/testing.rs`, used by `editor/artifact_tests.rs` and `api/owner/artifact_tests.rs`, re-implementing the proof module's own tint), and `BoundModule` and `TestModule` in the registry's tests; the artifact tests should use the proof module instead of `TintModule`.

Discovery being inert (no file, thread or Keychain touched by listing or reopening) is shown more than once, as in `discovery_status_and_reopen_start_no_lane_reach_no_network_and_create_nothing` and `the_proof_module_and_its_task_method_are_discovered_without_any_side_effect`, and a sentinel-secret redaction scan several times; each needs one owner. Near-identical owner test harnesses exist in `lifecycle_tests.rs` and `proof_tests.rs`, each with its own `mutation` helper. The shared `JsonDocument` (`capabilities/document.rs`) is exercised only through its three callers, settings, grants and installed resources, with no test of its own.

One property is tested once per layer (unit, service, owner/JSON, process, desktop, rendered); a second test at the same layer must say what the first one misses that justifies it. Each deleted assertion is named, in the commit, with the kept test that proves it: a test that cannot fail is deleted or rewritten, never kept as coverage. The core's own test clean-up gives the crate one `mutation` helper; the capability tests adopt it.
